known_for: Casinos, boardwalk entertainment, and seaside dining
about: Atlantic City is New Jersey's entertainment capital, famous for its iconic mile-long boardwalk lined with casinos, restaurants, and shops. Spring break is an ideal time to visit — crowds are smaller than summer but the beaches are opening up and hotel rates are still below peak-season prices. Students can gamble at world-class casinos, catch live shows, and indulge in some of the best seafood on the East Coast.

known_for: Victorian architecture, whale watching, and a historic National Landmark District
about: Cape May is one of the oldest seaside resorts in the United States and a National Historic Landmark District. Its streets are lined with over 600 preserved Victorian homes painted in pastel hues, making it feel like a living museum. Spring is prime whale and dolphin watching season, and the Cape May Spring Festival fills the town with birding events and food tours well before the summer crowds arrive.
attractions: Sunset Beach and Cape May diamonds

known_for: Free beach, Doo Wop architecture, and a 38-block amusement boardwalk
about: Wildwood is pure Jersey Shore nostalgia — America's largest free beach, a retro neon-lit boardwalk stretching 38 blocks, and three amusement piers with over 100 rides. The 1950s-60s Doo Wop motel architecture gives the town a pop-art identity unlike anywhere else. Spring is great because parking is free, coasters open for the season, and the beach is uncrowded.

known_for: Spring break vibe, Casino Pier coasters over the ocean, and MTV Jersey Shore filming location
about: Seaside Heights is the quintessential college spring break destination. Casino Pier juts dramatically over the ocean with roller coasters, the boardwalk buzzes with arcades and food stands, and the dense apartment scene makes for budget-friendly group rentals. It gained pop culture fame from MTV's Jersey Shore filmed right on the boardwalk, but the actual town is a lively shore community with great people-watching.
attractions: Casino Pier (roller coasters over the ocean)

known_for: Live music, Art Deco boardwalk, and a vibrant creative scene
about: Asbury Park is New Jersey's most eclectic beach city — a once-declining resort reborn as a hub for indie music, craft food, and an LGBTQ+-welcoming culture. The Stone Pony is one of America's most legendary live-music venues (Bruce Springsteen's home stage), and the Art Deco Convention Hall anchors a newly revitalized beachfront. Spring is ideal: concert season kicks off, beach bars open, and you beat the packed summer crowds.
attractions: The Stone Pony (legendary live music venue)
Asbury Park Boardwalk and Convention Hall
Cookman Avenue dining, art galleries and shops
Deal Lake waterfront and canoe launch

known_for: 18-mile barrier island with quiet beaches, Old Barney lighthouse, and fresh seafood
about: Long Beach Island is an 18-mile-long barrier island connected to the mainland by a single causeway, giving it a true island getaway feel. The charming town of Beach Haven anchors the south end with boutiques, restaurants, and an amusement park. The Barnegat Lighthouse (Old Barney) offers stunning panoramic views, and spring brings the island back to life before summer crowds and summer prices hit.
attractions: Beach Haven shops, bars and restaurants
Long Beach Island Foundation of the Arts

known_for: Family-friendly dry town, 2.5-mile boardwalk, and Shriver's salt water taffy
about: Ocean City calls itself America's Greatest Family Resort and has been a dry (no-alcohol) town since 1879, giving it a unique atmosphere on the Jersey Shore. The 2.5-mile boardwalk is lined with pizza shops, taffy stores, and amusement rides. Spring brings the Doo Dah Parade and the start of boardwalk food season before summer traffic hits, making it a relaxed and affordable visit.
attractions: Cape May County Park and Zoo (free)

known_for: Free national park beaches, America's oldest lighthouse (1764), and Fort Hancock
about: Sandy Hook is a 6-mile barrier spit managed by the National Park Service as part of Gateway National Recreation Area. It offers some of the most pristine beaches on the Jersey Shore for free, plus Fort Hancock (an 1890s Army post) and the oldest operating lighthouse in the US (built 1764). It is the ultimate budget destination — pack your own food and the whole day costs almost nothing.
attractions: Sandy Hook Lighthouse (oldest operating in the US, built 1764)
New York City skyline views across the bay

known_for: Princeton University, Ivy League campus architecture, and Einstein's hometown
about: Princeton offers a completely different kind of spring break — an Ivy League college town packed with world-class architecture, renowned free museums, and excellent independent restaurants and coffee shops. Strolling the Princeton University campus costs nothing, the art museum has no admission fee, and Witherspoon Street's dining scene punches above its weight. Albert Einstein lived and worked here and his former home on Mercer Street is a quiet pilgrimage.
attractions: Albert Einstein's former house on Mercer Street

known_for: Appalachian Trail, spring waterfalls, and Delaware River outdoor recreation
about: Delaware Water Gap National Recreation Area spans 70,000 acres of northwest New Jersey and northeast Pennsylvania, offering world-class outdoor adventure at remarkably low cost. The Appalachian Trail passes right through and the views from Mt. Tammany looking down at the river are among the best in the Mid-Atlantic. Spring is ideal — waterfalls like Dingmans Falls run at full power from snowmelt, wildflowers bloom, and trails are almost empty compared to summer.
attractions: Mt. Tammany summit hike (panoramic Delaware River views)
